A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IGL-Bench and contain readable main text, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–F. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite additions, renumbering, and formatting changes.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original classification experiments, imbalance sensitivity tests, embedding visualizations, and runtime and memory measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds ogbg-molhiv results, including classification scores and resource-limit failures.

M1.justification: The benchmark framework and its 24 integrated IGL algorithms remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish changes to their architectures, objectives, or training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: v3 adds ogbg-molhiv, increasing coverage from 16 to 17 datasets. This adds a larger collection of molecular graphs with natural class imbalance and biological-activity labels; the original datasets and node/graph classification tasks remain.

E2.justification: Table A.3 and corresponding experimental comparisons retain the same IGL methods and GCN/GIN comparators. The added dataset extends existing comparisons; newly cited methods such as Iceberg are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendices B.5–B.6 introduce sampling protocols for naturally imbalanced ogbg-molhiv, including balanced validation/test sets for class-imbalance evaluation. Figure B.1 revises reported training-class distributions, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun. Table D.23 also changes its stated metric from Micro-F1 to Macro-F1 while retaining existing scores.

E4.justification: Tables D.21–D.24 extend graph-size imbalance sensitivity testing to ogbg-molhiv at Low, Mid, and High levels. Only GIN has numerical outcomes; SOLT-GNN and TopoImb encounter resource limits. Existing robustness plots, embedding analyses, and efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten random runs and report means with standard deviations in Appendix C.1 and the result tables. Error-bar practices remain unchanged; revised numerical uncertainties do not establish a different statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds ogbg-molhiv outcomes and substantially revises selected existing scores. At the reported class-imbalance ratio of 100, GraphSMOTE's PubMed accuracy changes from 47.97±0.76 to 69.12±0.22 in Table D.1, and Macro-F1 changes from 34.78±0.80 to 63.27±0.19 in Table D.3. Other entries also change, and some repeated main/appendix results become inconsistent. These are substantial revisions to the reported empirical record; their cause is not established.

T1.justification: The mathematical substance of Definitions 1–2, imbalance equations B.1–B.6, and metric formulas C.1–C.4 is retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion expand the stated benchmark coverage from 16 to 17 datasets. The central contributions remain the first unified IGL benchmark, multifaceted evaluation of 24 algorithms, and an open-source package.

C2.justification: v1 calls node class imbalance and global topology imbalance orthogonal; v3's RQ2 insights qualify them as not entirely orthogonal. v3 also adds a homophily-based explanation for TOPOAUC's limitations and emphasizes distribution-shift generalization and graph foundation models in future directions. Appendix F.2's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Table B.2 supplies explicit per-class training counts, and v3 documents ogbg-molhiv statistics, licensing, and sampling details. Appendix C.2 newly states that model weights were saved across experimental settings. Hardware, hyperparameter search spaces, and package access information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references concerning graph foundation models, recent imbalance methods, and GC-Bench, while replacing several introductory graph-learning citations. Appendix F.1 retains its comparison with the same three surveys and its original benchmark positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds introduction and metric-selection explanations, introduces RQ insight summaries, and rewrites future directions. It replaces the checklist with an appendix contents page and updates author/publication information. The overall section organization and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: v3 duplicates the existing imbalance-definition table in the main text, adds sample-count and metric-survey tables, and expands graph-result tables with ogbg-molhiv columns. Figure B.1 is revised and Figure 6 gains imbalance-type labels. Conference headers, boxed insights, and colored best scores change presentation, while most analytical figures are reused.

improvement.justification: The added naturally imbalanced evaluation, explicit sample counts, and repaired CiteSeer/PubMed panels in Figure B.1 improve coverage and documentation. However, v3 introduces conflicting results: GraphSMOTE's Computers accuracy agreed at 76.04 in v1, but becomes 70.54 in v3 Table 2 while remaining 76.04 in Table D.1. ImGKB's REDDIT-B and ogbg-molhiv values are also reversed between Tables 5 and D.13. These reliability losses counterbalance the additions, leaving the net quality improvement unclear.
